task_brief: This is day 3 of "Art and Music Around Us". That is unit 5 in grade 3. Today is a guided practice (first pass) about respectful listening to new music. It takes about 40–60 minutes. It is one day's work, not the whole unit project. Your unit is working toward this: Create a small collection connecting a personal experience to one visual and one musical example. Today helps by working on respectful listening to new music. Your unit also covers art and music in daily life, community traditions, respectful listening to new music, and respectful looking at new art. Today adds real evidence toward your unit project.
primary_task: Make two small studies about respectful listening to new music. You may look at the example while you work. After each one, write the choice you made. Write what you wanted it to do. Keep both studies even if you do not like them. They show your process. Then circle the one move you could not do without the example. You will test that next time. This work stays private unless you want to share it. Use the attached Manuel Academy resource in this package. It gives you the model, example, or help sheet needed for this task. Keep today's work tied to your unit. Today is about respectful listening to new music. It is part of "Art and Music Around Us". ATTACHED MANUEL ACADEMY LEARNER RESOURCE

Resource ID: ma-resource:ma-g3-arts-music-u05-l03

Lesson focus: respectful listening to new music

Resource type: ACADEMY_CREATED_SCAFFOLD

GUIDED SCAFFOLD A — Use two four-pulse grids. In each box write or tap TA, TI-TI, rest, or hold. State an intent, point or perform through it, and circle the event creating the effect. In grid 2 change one box only. Mark the result same, stronger, or weaker and give one reason. Circle the step you still need prompted. Use it to study respectful listening to new music; describe evidence before judging and adapt the example rather than copying a finished work.

How to use it: Use the attached Manuel Academy resource in this package. It gives you the model, example, or help sheet needed for this task.

Rights: Manuel Academy original; licensed CC BY 4.0 for learner use and adaptation. No third-party text, image, score, lyric, melody, recording, or performance is included.

Access and materials: Household-accessible route: pencil or pen and scrap paper are enough. For sound or performance work, tap, clap, use spoken syllables, move a finger, or notate silently. Specialized art materials, instruments, paid software, cameras, microphones, and recording devices are optional and never affect credit.
critique_criteria: You made two studies with the example nearby and kept both.
Each one says the choice you made and what you wanted it to do.
You circled one move you could not do without the example.
Your work stayed private, seen only by you and maybe one trusted grown-up.

presentation_and_privacy.presentation_options: You choose the audience. Keeping the work entirely to yourself, showing it to one parent or trusted adult, or submitting it as a file with no one watching are all full-credit options. No public performance, exhibition, class presentation, live audience, photograph, camera, or voice recording is required at any point in this task, and choosing the most private option never lowers the score.
presentation_and_privacy.text_or_no_audio_alternative: A written alternative is always available and scores the same. Instead of performing, speaking, or recording, you may submit a written description of what you made or would make, a notated or diagrammed version, a labelled plan, or a written analysis covering the same criteria. Nothing in this task requires a working microphone, camera, or the ability to perform aloud.

copyright_and_authorship: The graded submission must be your own authorship. A parent, tutor, or AI tool may explain an idea, demonstrate a technique, or give feedback on a draft, but must not produce, write, debug, or make any part of the work that is scored. Any material you did not create yourself must be in the public domain, openly licensed, or used as a short cited excerpt for study — reproduce no more than the point requires, credit the maker and the source, and never copy full lyrics, a complete score, or a whole image and present it as your own.
accessibility_options: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.
Allow typed, handwritten, spoken, drawn, manipulatives-based, or demonstrated responses when the standard permits.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, movement-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for media.
Preserve the learning target while adjusting quantity, pacing, representation, or response mode.
task_accessibility_provisions: This task uses sound (respectful listening to new music). You do not have to hear it to do it. You may use a written or drawn version, feel the beat by tapping or watching, or read the notes on paper instead.
You can take a break, stretch, or come back to this later. That does not lower your score.
safety_and_privacy_rules: Allow a pause, break, or alternate response mode without treating it as failure.
Protect hearing, ventilation, tool safety, copyright, cultural context, and respectful representation.
No public performance, voice recording, photo, or camera use is ever required; provide a private, written, or no-audio alternative for every task.
Use only original student work, public-domain material, or properly licensed excerpts; never reproduce full copyrighted lyrics, sheet music, or protected works.
The final product must remain the student’s own authorship; adult or AI assistance may support planning and feedback but must not create the graded work.

media.suggestion: Optional diagram, map, worked example, source image, demonstration, or short clip supporting respectful listening to new music.
media.fallback: Provide the same information as readable steps, alt text, transcript, tactile/concrete model, or teacher demonstration.

remediation: Reteaching for respectful listening to new music follows the signal actually observed, not a fixed script. If the signal is "prerequisite gap": Return to the smallest prerequisite needed for respectful listening to new music, model it with a concrete or text-only representation, then retry one fresh item. If the signal is "procedure without understanding": Ask the learner to explain or represent why the process for respectful listening to new music works before continuing. If the signal is "correct but low confidence": Confirm the reasoning specifically, offer one varied example of respectful listening to new music, and avoid unnecessary remediation. If the signal is "repeated error pattern": Name the observable pattern neutrally, contrast it with a worked example, and schedule a short same-day or next-session review. If the signal is "mastery evidence": Require accurate independent application plus explanation on a later or different occasion before marking respectful listening to new music mastered. Re-check with one fresh item of the same kind before moving on, and record which signal was seen so the pattern is visible across the unit rather than treated as a one-off.
extension: Apply respectful listening to new music under a new constraint, compare two approaches or perspectives, or teach the idea with an original example without completing another learner’s graded work. Treat this as optional depth on respectful listening to new music rather than extra volume: one harder case done well beats three more of the same. Extension work stays private by default and uses only original, public-domain, or properly cited material. Extension work is never required to reach mastery and must not be assigned as a penalty.
